anomalies.observed: A 74LVC1G34 single-gate buffer (U5) sits on the top sheet. Its input is labelled "Troj_SCL_IN" and a diagonal wire runs from that input to the PB8/PB9 area of U2, which is the NFC_SCL/NFC_SDA I2C path. Its output runs to an off-sheet label beginning "Tro...". The part is not listed anywhere in the specification's component table or interface description.
anomalies.expected: The NFC I2C lines should connect directly from U2 (PB8 = NFC_SCL, PB9 = NFC_SDA) to U3 (SCL pin 3, SDA pin 5), with the pull-ups R1/R2 as the only added elements. The spec's component table and netlist description name no buffer or logic IC, and state that no MCU or other active IC besides U2, U3 and U4 appears.

evidence.quote: U5 74LVC1G34 ... "Troj_SCL_IN" and "Tro..." off-sheet label on the top sheet (Id 1/3), with the diagonal wire from U5's input landing on the PB8/PB9 pins of U2
The schematic does not show where VCC is generated... No MCU other than U2 appears.
NFC_SCL net: U2 pin 61 (PB8) — R2 (10 kΩ) to VCC — U3 pin 3 (SCL)

anomalies.impact: An unlisted logic gate inserted into the NFC I2C clock path can corrupt, delay or mirror the SCL signal, or route it off-board to an unintended net. This is a likely hardware-tampering or trojan insertion, and it would break or covertly leak NFC/PSBT communication.
